crm_notes:
Top-line: Stratum is a fintech analytics provider building a conversational research assistant + semantic similarity pipelines for SEC filings and market data. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable unit economics and strict residency/KMS requirements. Team wants detailed reserved capacity cost model that ties commitment level to per-token unit economics and shows sensitivity to utilization.

Recent asks / quotes: 
- "Can we model committed 6, 12, 24-month options with utilization brackets (40/60/80%) and show effective $/1k tokens, plus break-even vs hosted API" (Finance -> Ethan)
- Need clear fallback strategy: routing to smaller quantized variants when capacity spike > 85% utilization.

Numbers shared on call (customer-provided telemetry):
- Peak daily tokens: 48M tokens (30-day replay), typical day: 22M tokens, monthly projected canonical: 650M tokens.
- Critical workloads: real-time chat (p95 target 150ms for 64-token responses), and nightly embedding bulk jobs (throughput > 200k vectors/hour).

POC notes:
- POC run used 4-node config (H100-equivalent): sustained 1800 tokens/sec aggregate in batching mode; average GPU utilization ~62% during synthetic peak window.
- Observed tail latency at concurrency spikes; Redwood team suggested KV prefix caching + policy-based routing to smaller quantized fallback model to keep p95 SLA.

Decision factors called out by buyer:
- Cost predictability (finance) > 1st priority, then data residency/KMS (security), then latency SLOs for chat.
- Will consider 12-month commit if unit economics show >=30% reduction vs on-demand public cloud.

Action items:
- Deliver revised cost-model workbook (see linked drive) with three commit levels, utilization sensitivity, and waterfall of token-level unit costs.
- Legal to get draft SLA with credit schedule; security to validate KMS integration pattern.
- SE to run a second POC measurement at 128-token context by 2026-03-18.

Notes phrasing style: shorthand bullets, quotes from CFO: "we need forward-looking clarity on cost per 1k tokens across low/high season".
unit_economics_summary: Summary of modeling provided to customer: three commitment buckets modeled (Conservative: 2 reserved nodes, Typical: 4 reserved nodes, Aggressive: 8 reserved nodes). Assumptions: H100-equivalent GPU pricing amortized; monthly reserved cost (example) Conservative=$12,000, Typical=$40,000, Aggressive=$78,000. Utilization scenarios at 40%, 60%, 80%. Effective cost per 1k tokens (example outcomes): Conservative @60% -> $0.22/1k, Typical @60% -> $0.071/1k, Aggressive @60% -> $0.037/1k. Sensitivity: +/-10% utilization changes per-1k cost by ~12-15%. Compared to hosted API baseline provided by customer ($0.12/1k for mixed chat+embedding workload) the Typical 12-month commit reaches parity at ~58% utilization and saves ~40% at 75% utilization.
reserved_capacity_plan: Proposed reserved footprint: 4 H100-equivalent GPUs (typical) as initial commit; scale to 8 GPUs if sustained 30-day avg utilization >70%. Autoscaling/burst policy: dedicated pool with 2-node burst to public cloud for spikes above 85% (cost noted in blended model). Rolling deploy policy: canary 10% of traffic to new model build; automatic fallback to quantized variant (Q4_8bit) when avg queue depth > threshold. Billing model for customer: monthly reservation invoice + overage metered at a blended per-token uplift. Financial ask: 6/12/24 month commit pricing tiers included in workbook.
sla_requirements: Stated SLA targets required by Stratum: 99.5% availability for dedicated pool, p95 generation latency <=150ms for 64-token responses, throughput target 220 req/s sustained, error rate <0.2% per month. Contractual asks: uptime credits in 0.5% increments, data residency + audit logging retention 7 years (legal/finance will push for 10-year retention for some logs). Redwood action: confirm SLA credit bands and provide ops runbook for incident escalation.
tech_requirements_summary: Key technical constraints: customer-managed KMS for model inputs/outputs at rest, SAML SSO for console and API access, VPC peering to customer network, optional air-gapped packaging for sensitive subsets. Model preferences: prefer open LlamaX variants and smaller quantized fallback; routing rules must support model variant affinity by route (chat -> low-latency model; batch embeddings -> high-throughput model). Metrics required: per-token cost breakdown, GPU utilization by hour, p95/p99 latency histograms, cache hit ratios.
